newsitem.title: USA: DHL to open two LatAm logistics centers.
newsitem.headline: DHL to open two LatAm logistics centers.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express expects to open two logistics centers in Latin America early in the second quarter of 1997, a company official told Reuters this week.
"We see the future to be very bright for logistics in Latin America," said Umberto Gonzalez, regional logistics manager for Latin America.

The centers in Panama City and Sao Paulo are expected to open in April, he said. The Panama center will start at 2,000 square meters and the Brazil at 1,000 square meters, although both can be expanded to 10,000 square meters, Gonzalez said.
"We will do third party logistics and help companies with their distribution in Latin America," said Gonzalez.
Worldwide, the privately-held company has four other logistics centers.

Many multi-national companies are outsourcing their warehousing and distribution operations, and companies like DHL are taking on those tasks. Just-in-time manufacturing operations also have prompted the growth of logistics.
"When an item is in the logistics center in Panama, I can deliver it overnight to 32 countires," said Gonzalez.

"A company can send a computer in parts and our technicians will put it together and test it and deliver it," he said, "We can even pick up your broken computer and fix it and deliver it back to you."
DHL, with a long history in Latin America, has 160 offices and more than 2,300 employees there.

The new DHL logistics centers in Latin America will likely handle high technology equipment, consumer electronics, repair parts and medical equipment and supplies and other items. "We expect a large spectrum of goods," Gonzalez said.
